quick_read.weather_md: **Weather:** 13°C high / 8°C low. Wind always. Sun until midnight, then twilight, then sun again — true midnight sun. Waterproof layer, not optional, any month.
quick_read.uv_md: **UV:** Low number, 4 — deceptive. **21 hours of daylight means pale skin burns fast.** SPF 30+ broad spectrum on face + hands every morning. Eye mask for sleeping, sweet one — the sun does not really set.
quick_read.uv_advisory_md: *📎 Goose Investigation Bureau — sourcing UV from EPA + Cancer Research UK. UV 1–2 = no protection needed. UV 3+ = sunscreen + shade + hat + sunglasses. UV 8+ = limit midday sun. UV 11+ = stay out of midday sun entirely.*
quick_read.budget_hint_md: **Daily budget — $290 average.** With my picks below, that's real. Iceland is genuinely expensive — restaurants run 50% above Western Europe. Save: cook one meal at the guesthouse, walk instead of taxi (Reykjavik is small). Splurge: whale tour + Michelin night.
quick_read.intro_md: > *Sweet one, I know the hardest part of this trip was leaving your fur baby behind. Iceland's pet rules don't allow tourists to bring animals — but the country will give you so much animal love back: whales, puffins, Icelandic horses, and Reykjavik's famous cats. Below is the full goose investigation. Soft landing for a soft heart.*
quick_read.do_now_md:
**Do now:**
- **Book whale-watching from Old Harbor, morning slot.** Calmer seas before noon, ~90% sighting rate in June. Minkes and humpbacks are the typical sightings; orcas appear occasionally. Iceland is one of the few places left where you can see wild whales ethically.
- **Pack layers — windproof outer, fleece middle, base layer.** Weather flips in 20 minutes. Sunny → driving rain → sunny again. June isn't the exception.
- **Cards everywhere, almost no cash needed.** Iceland is one of the most cashless countries on earth. Apple Pay and Google Pay clear at hot-dog stands. Pull 5,000 ISK (~$35) for emergencies and that's it.
quick_read.restaurant_hook_md: **The Places to Eat list below is the play.** Real food. Some Michelin Guide, none gold-card. Iceland's restaurant scene punches above its size — Dill is a one-star New Nordic experience, the rest is exceptional comfort food. Book Dill 8+ weeks ahead; the rest can be week-of.

happening.news_md:
- **🌋 Volcano watch — Reykjanes peninsula.** Last eruption ended August 5, 2025. As of April 2026, the magma reservoir under Grindavík is at its highest level since the 2023 eruption series began. Scientists expect another eruption "in coming weeks or months." Important context, sweet one: **the previous nine eruptions did not disrupt flights, did not affect Reykjavik, did not close the Ring Road.** Iceland is safe to visit during volcanic activity. The Icelandic Met Office monitors 24/7; check `safetravel.is` the day you arrive. [src 1]
- **Bridge closure — Jökulsá á Fjöllum, May 26 – Jun 16, 8am-7pm.** Road work. Only matters if you're driving the full Ring Road during your first week; Golden Circle day trips unaffected. [src 1]
- **Pet rules — tourists cannot bring pets.** Full stop. Only relocation with import permit + microchip + multiple vaccinations. So your fur baby stays home and waits. Sorry I keep saying it; I know it stings. [src 2]
happening.sports_md: - **🐎 Icelandic horse stables — Þingvellir area, ~$90 per ride.** Two-hour rides on the fifth-gait Icelandic horse (the *tölt*, a smooth gallop that only this breed has). Local stables run morning + afternoon trips. Real animal-time on the trip.
happening.entertainment_md:
- **🎵 Secret Solstice festival — ~Jun 18–21 (2026 dates TBC).** Midnight-sun music festival in Laugardalur Park, walkable from city center. Three days of stages running through the bright night, plus side events: a concert inside the Langjökull glacier and a geothermal pool party. Lineup mixes Icelandic acts (Sigur Rós and Of Monsters and Men have played) with international indie/electronic/hip-hop. Confirm dates at `secretsolstice.is`. [src 3]
- **🎨 Reykjavik Arts Festival.** Typically late May into early June, mixed-media — opera, theatre, contemporary art across the city. Check `listahatid.is` for the 2026 program. [src 4]
- **☀️ Summer solstice — Jun 21.** Longest day of the year, 21+ hours of daylight, sun never fully sets. Locals stay out until 3am because they can. Hike Mount Esja in the evening for sunset-that-isn't.

brief.watch_md:
- **Whale watching from Old Harbor — ~$90 per ticket.** Morning slot is calmer seas. Minkes and humpbacks most common, orcas occasionally. Combined whale + puffin tours add an hour, see Akurey and Lundey puffin colonies. Animal-lover bucket-list, done right. [src 5]
- **Sundhöll Reykjavíkur — ~$7 entry.** Niche pick, sweet one, and I cannot stress this enough. Old downtown thermal pool, opened 1937, designed by the architect of Hallgrímskirkja. Locals' anchor — the real Icelandic social life, not Blue Lagoon. Bring swimsuit, shower naked beforehand (rule, not suggestion), then float in 38°C geothermal water under the midnight sun. Maximum culture-meets-warmth.
- **Sun Voyager sculpture at midnight — FREE.** Iconic steel longboat skeleton on the fjord shore. Low sun = surreal light. Photo: Sæbraut shoreline path, around 11pm in June.
- **Hallgrímskirkja tower — ~$8 entry.** Lift to the top of the iconic concrete church. Full Reykjavik panorama: painted houses, mountains, ocean. Photo: top platform looking east toward harbor.
- **Þingvellir National Park — FREE entry, ~$80 day-rental car.** Walk between two tectonic plates (literally). Golden Circle staple. Niche addition: site of the world's first parliament (930 AD). Icelandic horses graze the open fields — calm spot for missing your fur baby from a distance.
brief.eat_md:
*Most are Guide-listed, not starred. Real food, no gold-card spectacle.*

- **Dill** — One Michelin star. New Nordic, foraging-driven. Tasting menu only. Book 8+ weeks ahead. *(~$160 pp tasting menu)*
- **Sumac** — Guide listed. Middle-Eastern lamb-shoulder mash-up, easier same-week booking. *(~$45-65)*
- **Matur og Drykkur** — Guide listed. Modern takes on Icelandic classics — cod head, salted lamb, fermented shark for the brave. *(~$50-70)*
- **Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur** — Not Michelin, but every Icelandic local + Bill Clinton has stood here. Famous hot-dog stand. *(~$5 a dog)*
brief.knowing_md:
- **Tap water is the best in Europe.** Free, glacial, ice-cold. Hotel restaurants look offended if you order bottled. Refill your bottle anywhere.
- **Weather flips fast.** Sunny → driving rain in 20 minutes. Carry your shell always. Don't trust hourly forecasts beyond 3 hours.
- **Reykjavik's "cats rule the city."** Dogs were banned in Reykjavik from 1924 to 1984 to stop disease transmission. The cats took over and never left. You'll see them on every street, often with collars (they belong to someone), often with their own Instagram. The closest you'll get to dog-petting on this trip, sweet one.
- **Tipping not expected.** Service is included. Round up if exceptional, but nothing else is required.
- **Pools are religion.** Every neighborhood has one. Locals go 2–3 times a week. Sundhöll downtown, Vesturbæjarlaug west side, Laugardalslaug for the biggest. ~$7 entry. Bring swimsuit + flip-flops. Pre-shower naked or you will be told off. Worth every awkward moment.

budget_usd.notes: Mid = guesthouse or 3-star ($170), 2 meals out ($75), whale tour or day-rental ($45). Iceland runs 50% above Western Europe for restaurants.
